questions.question: The SEVA app was launched by which of the following ministers to track coal dispatch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Piyush Goyal**__

__
 
• ** SEVA App:- **

 
 
• The SEVA app was launched in 2018 as a part of the Digital India initiative.
 
• **It is a mobile app that allows users to track the dispatch of coal from Coal India Limited (CIL) to power plants.**
 
• The app provides information on the quantity of coal dispatched, the date of dispatch, and the mode of transport.
 
• **The SEVA app was launched by Piyush Goyal, the Union Minister of State (IC) for Power, Coal, New & Renewable Energy and Mines.**
 
• The SEVA app is aimed at increasing transparency and accountability in the coal dispatch process.
 
• It also helps to ensure that power plants have a reliable supply of coal, which is essential for uninterrupted power generation.

• **He was an Indian politician who served as the Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution in the Union Cabinet of India from 2014 to 2020. **
 
• He was the founder and president of the Lok Janshakti Party (LJP), a political party in India that represents the interests of the Dalit community.
 
 
 
• **Nitin Gadkari:-**
 
 
• **He is an Indian politician who is the current Minister for Road Transport & Highways in the Government of India. **
 
• He is also the longest serving Minister for Road Transport & Highways currently running his tenure for over 9 years.

• He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

questions.question: Which among the following Vedas is the oldest?

• **The Rigveda is a collection of hymns and prayers that are sung in praise of the Vedic gods.**

questions.question: __________was introduced during fifth five year plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minimum Needs Programme.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minimum Needs Programme:-**

 
 
• **The Minimum Needs Programme (MNP) was launched in India in 1974-75 as part of the Fifth Five-Year Plan. **
 
• It was a comprehensive social development programme aimed at providing basic essential amenities to the poor and underserved sections of the population.
 
• The MNP covered a wide range of sectors, including:
 
 
• **Rural health**
 
• **Rural water supply**
 
• **Rural electrification**
 
• **Elementary education**
 
• **Adult education**
 
• **Nutrition**
 
• **Environmental improvement of urban slums**
 
• **Houses for landless labourers**
 
 
 
• **The MNP was implemented by the central government in collaboration with the state governments. **
 
• The central government provided financial assistance to the states, while the states were responsible for planning and implementing the programme.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao:-**

 
 
• **BBBP is a flagship program of the Government of India launched in January 2015. **
 
• It is a tri-ministerial effort of the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health & Family Welfare and Human Resource Development.
 
• The scheme aims to address the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of women empowerment over a life-cycle continuum.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:-**
 
 
• **It is a nationwide campaign launched by the Government of India in 2014 to improve sanitation and hygiene conditions in India. **
 
• The campaign aims to achieve the vision of a 'Clean India' by eliminating open defecation and improving solid waste management.

questions.question: MSME stands for small and ___________ enterprises.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**medium-sized **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **MSME:-**

 
 
• **It stands for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. **
 
• It is a sector of the Indian economy that consists of enterprises engaged in the production, manufacturing, processing or preservation of goods and services, whose investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed the limit specified for the sector.
 
• The MSME sector is classified into three categories based on their investment in plant and machinery or equipment:
 
 
• **Micro:** Investment up to INR 25 lakh
 
• **Small**: Investment between INR 25 lakh and INR 10 crore
 
• **Medium**: Investment between INR 10 crore and INR 50 crore
 
 
 
• The MSME sector plays a vital role in the Indian economy.** It contributes around 45% of India's GDP and employs over 11 crore people. The sector is also responsible for over 40% of India's exports.**
 
• The Government of India has implemented a number of schemes and initiatives to support the MSME sector. These include:
 
 
• **Udyam Registration:** A free and online registration process for MSMEs to get a unique identification number (Udyam Registration Number).
 
• **Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)**: Provides credit guarantees to MSMEs to help them access loans from banks and financial institutions.
 
• **Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):** A self-employment scheme for educated unemployed youth to set up micro-enterprises.
 
• **MSME Development Institutes (MSMEDIs): **Provide various training and support services to MSMEs.

questions.question: The maximum inflation in India was recorded in the year ___________ at 25.2 per cent was mainly attributed to the failure of kharif crops in the previous year and also to the hike in crude oil prices in the previous year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1974-75**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The maximum inflation in India was recorded in the year 1974-75 at 25.2 per cent. **
 
• **It was mainly attributed to the failure of kharif crops in the previous year and also to the hike in crude oil prices in the previous year.**
 
• The failure of kharif crops led to a shortage of food supply in the country, which pushed up food prices.
 
• The hike in crude oil prices, on the other hand, increased the cost of transportation and other inputs, which further fueled inflation.
 
• In addition to the factors mentioned above, the high inflation rate in 1973 was also attributed to the following:
 
 
• **The Vietnam War**, which led to increased global demand for oil and other commodities, pushing up prices.
 
• **The global recession of 1973-74,** which led to a decline in demand for Indian exports, further weakening the rupee and pushing up import prices.
 
• **The government's expansionary fiscal policies**, which led to increased government spending and borrowing, which also contributed to inflation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation:-**

 
 
• **It is the rate at which the prices of goods and services are rising in an economy. **
 
• It is typically measured as a percentage change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which is a basket of goods and services that households commonly purchase.
 
• Inflation can be caused by a number of factors, including:
 
 
• **Demand-pull inflation**: This occurs when there is too much money chasing too few goods and services. This can happen when the economy is growing rapidly and consumers have more money to spend.
 
• **Cost-push inflation: **This occurs when the cost of producing goods and services increases, leading to higher prices for consumers. This can happen due to factors such as rising wages, higher energy costs, or supply chain disruptions.
 
• **Built-in inflation**: This occurs when workers demand higher wages to keep up with rising prices. This can lead to a wage-price spiral, where wages and prices continue to chase each other higher.

questions.question: What is the emerging magma from a volcano onto the earth’s surface called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lava**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lava**__:-

 __
 
• **Lava is molten or partially molten rock (magma) that has been expelled from the interior of a terrestrial planet (such as Earth) or a moon onto its surface.**
 
• Lava may be erupted at a volcano or through a fracture in the crust, on land or underwater, usually at temperatures from 800 to 1,200 °C (1,470 to 2,190 °F).
 
• **The volcanic rock resulting from subsequent cooling is also often called lava. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ash:-**

 
 
• **It refers to the fine-grained material that is ejected from volcanoes during eruptions. **
 
• It is made up of tiny fragments of rock, minerals, and volcanic glass.
 
• Ash can be carried long distances by winds, and it can have a significant impact on the environment. 
 
• Ash can be harmful to plants and animals. It can block sunlight, making it difficult for plants to photosynthesize.
 
• Ash can also contaminate water supplies and damage buildings and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Pyroclastic flows:-**
 
 
• **It is also known as pyroclastic density currents, are a type of volcanic hazard that consists of a high-density mixture of hot gases, ash, and rock fragments.**
 
• They can travel at speeds of up to 700 km/h and reach temperatures of up to 1,000 °C.
 
• Pyroclastic flows can be extremely destructive, and they have been responsible for some of the deadliest volcanic eruptions in history.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** 42nd Amendment Act:-**

 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the Mini-Constitution__ because of the enormous number of revisions it has made to the Indian Constitution.
 
• it was enacted in 1976 during an Emergency period by Indira Gandhi Government. 
 
• It is regarded as one of the most controversial amendment 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act commonly known Constitution Act of 1976.
 
• It amended and introduced various provisions in the Indian constitution given below:
 __
 
• It tries to curtail the power of the Supreme Court and the High Courts. 
 
• It added Part IVA (Fundamental Duties) in the constitution. 
 
• It added there new words in the preamble (Socialist, Secular and Integrity).
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• 44th Amendment Act:-

 
 
• It was introduced by the government in 1978 so that it can overturn the provisions of the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
 
 
• **41st Amendment:-**
 
 
• It was ratified on January 20, 1975.
 
• **It provides for the right to property and the right to compensation in case of compulsory acquisition of property.**
 
 
 
• **43rd Amendment:-**
 
 
• It was ratified on August 28, 1975.
 
• **It made sweeping changes to the Constitution, including the abolition of the right to property and the right to compensation in case of compulsory acquisition of property.**

questions.question: _______________ is an indicator used by experts to gauge the number of people dying prematurely due to a particular disease
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**global burden of diseases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Global Burden of Disease:-**

 
 
• GBD is the sum of all health loss from diseases, injuries, and risk factors across a population.
 
• **It is measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), which are a unit that combines years of life lost to premature death with years lived in disability.**
 
• The GBD study is the most comprehensive and widely used measure of global health.
 
• **It is conducted by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, and it is published annually in the Lancet medical journal.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Diseases:-**

 
 
• **GDD is a satirical term used to describe the negative consequences of economic growth, such as environmental degradation, income inequality, and social alienation. **
 
• It is a play on the term "gross domestic product" (GDP), which is a measure of the total value of all goods and services produced in a country within a given period of time.
 
 
 
• **Goods and services tax:-**
 
 
• **GST is a value-added tax (VAT) that is levied on most goods and services sold for domestic consumption. **
 
• The GST is paid by consumers, but it is remitted to the government by the businesses selling the goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Gross national product:-**
 
 
• **GNP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a nation's economy during a specific period of time (usually a year),** computed before allowance is made for the depreciation or consumption of capital used in the process of production.

questions.question: How many High Courts are there in India as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** High Courts:-**

 
 
• ​The institution of the high court originated in India in 1862 with three high courts set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
 
• The fourth HC was established in Allahabad in 1966.
 
• Currently, India has a total of 25 High Courts established in different states of the country.
 
• Andhra Pradesh HC became the 25th HC in India commencing from 1 Jan 2010 at Amaravati.
 
• The UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh have a common high court.
 
• Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers, procedures and so on of the HC.
 
• The Seventh Amendment Act of 1956 authorised the Parliament to establish a common HC for two or more states or two or more states and a UT
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jurisdiction of High Courts

 
 
• Bombay HC - Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu
 
• Guwahati HC - Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh
 
• Punjab and Haryana HC - Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh
 
• Calcutta HC - West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.question: When was the Harijan Sewak Sangh founded as a result of the Poona Pact?
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harijan Sevak Sangh:-**

 
 
• **It is a non-profit organization founded by Mahatma Gandhi on September 30, 1932, in Pune, India. **
 
• The organization's goal is to eradicate untouchability and uplift marginalized sections of society, such as Dalits, women, and children.
 
• The main activities of Harijan Sevak Sangh include:
 
 
• **Raising awareness against untouchability**
 
• **Socially and economically empowering Dalits**
 
• **Providing Dalits with access to education and healthcare services**
 
• **Fighting for the rights of Dalits**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Poona Pact:-**

 
 
• ​It was an **agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on behalf of Dalits, also known as depressed classes, and upper caste Hindu leaders on the reservation of electoral seats for the depressed classes in the legislature of British India in 1932.**
 
• It was made on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada Central Jail in Poona, India.
 
• It was signed by Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes and by Madan Mohan Malviya on behalf of upper caste Hindus, Faraz Shah, Sana Ejaz and Gandhi.

• She is an Indian field hockey player.

questions.question: In which of the following union territories was the highest literacy rate recorded in 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Literacy rate:-**

 
 
• The literacy rate is the total percentage of the population of an area at a particular time aged seven years or above who can read and write with understanding. 
 
• According to Census 2011 Lakshadweep, with a literacy rate of 92.28%, is the Union Territory with the highest literacy rate in India.
 
• The female literacy rate of Lakshadweep is 88.25%.
 
• Kerala ranks the highest in terms of literacy rate with a 93.91% literacy rate.

questions.question: Where will you find plastids in a leaf cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytoplasm**:-

 
 
• **Cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance that fills the inside of a cell. **
 
• It is composed of water, salts, and various organic molecules, including proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids.
 
• Cytoplasm also contains organelles, which are specialized structures that perform specific functions within the cell.
 
• **Plastids are found in the cytoplasm of leaf cells.**
 
• They are typically located in the mesophyll cells, which are the cells in the middle of the leaf blade. Mesophyll cells are specialized for photosynthesis, and plastids are the organelles where photosynthesis takes place.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Cell Membrane:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the plasma membrane, is a thin, flexible barrier that surrounds all cells.
 
• **It is made up of a double layer of phospholipids, which are molecules that have a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-fearing) tail.**
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:-**
 
 
• **The nucleus is the control center of the cell. **
 
• It is a spherical organelle that is surrounded by a double membrane.
 
• The nucleus contains the cell's genetic material, which is organized into chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall:-**
 
 
• **A cell wall is a rigid, external layer that surrounds some types of cells, just outside the cell membrane. **
 
• It can be tough, flexible, and sometimes rigid.
 
• It provides the cell with both structural support and protection, and also acts as a filtering mechanism.
